label: early original-phase input (t=2-5) with d/p/s/i/r/k/t after a q (diffuse)
explanation: 91% of activation mass falls in the original phase at t=2-5. It never fires at t=0-1 and almost never at the delimiter. It fires more when q (and less so a, l, 1, n) came earlier, especially two steps back (prev2_tok=q gives 8.6x lift; first_tok=q gives 4.9x), and when the current input is one of d, p, s, i, r, k, t. The top activations (about 0.25-0.30) are inputs such as p, r, s, d, t at t=3-4 after two q tokens (e.g. q q q r, a q a d). Copy-phase firing is weak and accounts for about 9% of the mass. The behaviour looks like a graded, additive mix of token identities rather than one crisp condition. The best simple predicate reaches only F1 of about 0.31 on dev (precision 0.39, mass recall 0.39). A broader seen-set version raises mass recall to 0.64 but lowers precision to 0.20. t=2-5 alone covers 88% of the mass at 3% precision.
